title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2611.32274v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) over long time horizons is computationally expensive using traditional numerical methods. While neural operators provide an efficient alternative, they suffer from the accumulation of approximation errors along the predicted trajectory, typically caused by the failure to capture fine-scale details. In this work, we design a Commutator Memory Neural Operator that identifies fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations and leverages these details to enhance the neural operator's capability in capturing fine-scale features over long time horizons. Specifically, we identify a performance gap between two operations: downsampling the high-resolution field before rollout prediction versus performing rollout prediction before downsampling. translated_abstract: 使用传统数值方法在长时间范围内求解非线性偏微分方程（PDE）的计算代价高昂。虽然神经算子提供了一种高效的替代方案，但它们在预测轨迹上会累积近似误差，这通常是由于未能捕捉细尺度细节所导致的。在这项工作中，我们设计了一种换位子记忆神经算子，它通过对两个操作进行换位来识别细尺度动力学细节，并利用这些细节来增强神经算子在长时间范围内捕捉细尺度特征的能力。具体而言，我们发现了两种操作之间的性能差距：一种是在滚动预测之前对高分辨率场进行下采样，另一种是先进行滚动预测再进行下采样。我们观察到，细尺度动力学细节往往编码在这一差距之中。通过换位这两个操作，细尺度细节能够被（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出换位子记忆神经算子（CoMNO），通过交换“先下采样后滚动预测”与“先滚动预测后下采样”两种操作顺序所产生的性能差距来提取细尺度动力学细节，从而增强神经算子在长时程偏微分方程预测中捕捉细尺度特征的能力。
en_tdlr: Proposes the Commutator Memory Neural Operator (CoMNO), which captures fine-scale dynamical details through the performance gap between commuting downsampling and rollout prediction operations, thereby enhancing neural operators' ability to capture fine-scale features in long-horizon PDE prediction.
